0x4058.name: plannedPositionAtStart
0x4058.note: Starting-grid slot consumed by the placement path (sub_4D10E0 -> sub_403CD0(gridTable, plannedPositionAtStart-1)). Prior art: moving a car on the grid requires writing this field AND vehicle+0x4060 together; writing only 0x4058 leaves the car on pole. Reviewed as a latched control input for the multiplayer qualifying-grid fix; writes must keep positions a contiguous 1..n permutation.

0x4060.name: position
0x4060.note: Race position ordered by standings and the visible grid; the second field required to move a car on the starting grid (see 0x4058). Reviewed as a latched control input for the multiplayer qualifying-grid fix; writes must keep positions a contiguous 1..n permutation.

0x44CC.name: PassingNorm
0x44CC.note: Baked AI Passing tuning input: .rcd Passing maps to 0.9 + Passing*0.001, capped at 1.0. AIRacingLine consumes it in the gap/line calculation; initialization may replace it. Game-thread temporary overrides must capture/restore by vehicle identity and session, use finite 0.9..1.0 values, and yield at session teardown. This is a latched tuning input, not computed scoring output.

0x44F8.name: TrackAggressionEffective
0x44F8.note: Baked AI follow-gap/pressure tuning input: AI Realism times TrackAggression, floored at 0.01 during initialization; AISteering consumes it without recomputing the input. Game-thread finite temporary controls require identity/session ownership and exact restoration. Classification does not authorize arbitrary ranges or make this a no-passing switch.

0x42D4.name: SteeringLaneMode0
0x42D4.note: Lane/conflict mode slot 0 in the five-entry 28-byte AISteering state array. Modes 1/2/7/8 reach Overtaking; mode 16 is the follow/fallback state. Read-only in the pass-commitment prototype.

0x42DC.name: SteeringLanePressure0
0x42DC.note: AISteering pass-pressure/history slot 0. Accumulates closing traffic weighted by TrackAggressionEffective, clamps to 0..450, and retains 85 percent on transition to mode 16. Live trace reproduced 450 to 382.5.

0x32C8.name: WearTickGate__was__slot_live_marker_
0x32C8.note: Controller/liveness role used by field construction: -1 inactive, 0 human, 1 AI, 2 remote. The multiplayer-AI prototype may temporarily park its own positively identified slots at -1 while stock network-slot cleanup runs, then restore 1 and rebuild the active pointer array on the same game-thread call. Never apply this to an unowned slot.

0x4538.name: MaxSpeed
0x4538.note: Not a raw poke: the field recalculates every frame, so the write is always the game's own ParameterValueSetter thiscall (a2 cast straight to float, 18 = pit-limit sentinel, 99999 = uncapped), re-armed every tick by the caller, gated on race_phase==5 the same as CallToBox. Never govern a car whose PitStatus (0x3450) != 0 -- that overwrites the game's own pit limiter.

0x0D58.name: RearWingIntactFlag
0x0D58.note: Width correction: the game tests and writes this as a byte. Zero plus CallToBox enters the game-owned garage/retirement path.

0x344C.name: PitEntryLatch
sources: findings.jsonl: pittingStatus full enum + pit-procedure companion offsets

0x3450.name: PitStatus
sources: findings.jsonl: pittingStatus full enum + pit-procedure companion offsets
findings.jsonl: web_telemetry pittingStatus int32 live proof
0x3450.note: State-machine output. Observe it; do not forge it to synthesize a stop.

0x3470.name: PitStopEndTime
0x3470.note: Written by the game when service becomes ready. A holder may re-arm it only after that write and should use now+lead, never +=lead.

0x413C.name: PitDecisionTimer
0x413C.note: Set to zero after scheduling a stop to make the AI evaluate the request.

DynMan_Restart.abi_evidence: Exact canonical SHA256 executable disassembled over 0x42C3B0..0x42C439 and caller Game_Restart. No incoming ECX/EDX or stack arguments are read; ECX is overwritten before use; return is EAX and plain C3 ret. Caller supplies no stack arguments (its ECX assignment is unused by this callee). First instruction is the complete five-byte push 0x26f (68 6F 02 00 00). Reviewed as no-argument cdecl; not authorized as a standalone arbitrary restart command. See tools/sdk/SAFETY_CAR_INTERFACE_REVIEW_2026-09-07.md.

AIDriverCountSetup.abi_evidence: The sole caller DynMan_Init pushes one path pointer and the callee returns with ret 4. The raw callee is stdcall, returns zero in eax, and is the last identity/count stage before DynMan_Init rebuilds the active array and runs its counted VehgenScnFileLoader loop. Canonical entry starts with the complete five-byte mov eax,[VehicleCount] instruction.

SuspensionForceComputationWithPerCornerV.abi_evidence: The sole caller RenderTickUpdate passes active_vehicle+20 in ecx with no stack arguments and consumes the byte result in al. The callee uses ecx as its dynamics owner, has no stack parameters, and returns a byte. Canonical entry begins with complete instructions 83 EC 24 56 8B F1.

DynMan_Init.abi_evidence: Raw function has no receiver or arguments; all call sites use a plain call. Canonical bytes begin with one complete six-byte stack-allocation instruction (81 EC 0C 02 00 00).

ProcessDriverEntries.abi_evidence: The two recovered callers pass the driver-entry manager in ecx with no stack arguments. The callee returns its final vehicle-bound pointer in eax. Canonical entry begins with one complete six-byte stack-allocation instruction.

MultiplayerQualificationGridAssignment.abi_evidence: The sole caller MultiplayerVehiclePlacement passes the session manager in ecx with no stack arguments and consumes the byte result in al. The callee uses the receiver throughout and returns the local-player-found byte. Canonical and reviewed DE151845 variant entries both begin with complete instructions 83 EC 10 55 56.

ConditionalFieldSetter.abi_evidence: Seven recovered callers pass the per-vehicle grid-state owner in ecx and one 32-bit position on the stack. The callee compares and writes that value and has no return value.

VehgenScnFileLoader.abi_evidence: Three callers pass a vehicle in ecx and one 32-bit stack argument; raw callee uses this and a byte value and returns a char pointer. Native safety-car load trials exercised this ABI on the game thread.

SceneRenderUpdate.abi_evidence: Seven recovered callers pass a vehicle in ecx and one 32-bit stack value consumed as a byte. The callee initializes physics, render, AI driver and collision state for that vehicle.

NetCommPlayerSlotSync.abi_evidence: Sole caller passes the network manager in ecx; callee has no stack arguments and returns its result in al. Canonical prologue preserves a thiscall frame.

VehicleLookupByName.abi_evidence: Raw callee and seven callers agree on stdcall with one path pointer; result is written to the canonical roster-index global.

NationalityDriverInfoLoader.abi_evidence: Confirmed F1CVehicle owner; raw callee and four callers agree on thiscall plus one roster-index argument. The same ABI was exercised by the native safety-car load-time prototype.

TeamIDSetter.abi_evidence: Raw twelve-line callee directly writes the one stack argument into five fields on the ecx vehicle. Two static callers and native safety-car live construction agree.

SessionStateTransition.abi_evidence: The explicit callers in NetCommPlayerSlotSync, RestartGate, and sub_4DA840 pass F1CVehicle+0x0C in ecx; ProcessDriverEntries constructs the same interior owner as v24+3 dwords. The callee reads its controller role at owner+0x32BC, which resolves to the canonical vehicle role at +0x32C8. Two 32-bit stack arguments are passed and the second is consumed as a byte. Passing the vehicle base corrupts the preceding controller field and is forbidden.
